name: Printing presses and print-on-demand
shape_facts: Offset, digital, large-format, screen/DTF, or a mix — and how many machines of each.
Mostly B2B (packaging, corporate, publishers) or walk-in/retail (cards, flex, wedding invitations).
In-house design team or customers bring ready files.
Number of jobs per day/week and typical run size (short runs vs long runs).
Whether post-press (lamination, die-cutting, binding, foiling) is in-house or outsourced.
Online POD channel or marketplace selling, and whether fulfilment is local or international.
Paper/board and ink bought on credit from a few dealers or imported.
scope_rule: pi notes problems with job flow, quoting, proof approvals, wastage, paper stock, reprints, receivables, delivery and staff. It does not advise on copyright or trademark questions (e.g. whether a customer may print a brand logo), election or political printing rules, currency or document printing legality, or colour-management engineering. It never stores customers’ artwork contents, guest lists from wedding cards, or personal details of the people whose names appear on printed items. Requests to print fake documents, certificates, receipts, stamps or counterfeit packaging are refused plainly.

vocabulary.job card: the slip that follows a job through the press
vocabulary.CTP / plate: printing plate made for each colour on offset
vocabulary.proof: sample sent to the customer for approval before the run
vocabulary.wastage sheets / setting: sheets lost while setting colours on the machine
vocabulary.die: cutting tool for boxes and labels
vocabulary.advance: deposit taken before starting a job

job flow: Where does a job usually get stuck — design, plates, printing or finishing?
Roughly how many jobs are open at any time?
How do you know a job’s status today?
quoting: How do you work out a quote now?
How often does the final cost come in above the quote?
proofs and reprints: How often do reprints happen in a month?
Who carries the cost when it happens?
wastage: Does anyone compare it job to job?
paper and board: Who decides when to reorder paper?
Have you run short mid-job recently?
How do counts in the godown compare with the register?
receivables: Which customers are slowest to pay?
How are advances recorded at the counter?
online/pod: How do they reach the shop floor?
staff: How do you know what each operator produced in a shift?
Has side-printing ever been a worry?

seasons: PK wedding season (October–March) drives cards and favours; Ramadan and Eid packaging and greeting runs; school and university session starts (books, registers, notebooks around March–April and August); calendar and diary season (November–January); election periods bring large flex/banner surges subject to rules. UAE: Ramadan and Eid packaging, National Day (2 December) branding, GITEX and trade-show season (October–March), back-to-school in late August. Canada: back-to-school, Black Friday and holiday POD peaks, tax-season form printing (February–April).
care: Refuse plainly any request to print fake degrees, IDs, stamps, receipts, currency or counterfeit brand packaging; pi notes nothing about it beyond declining.
Copyright/trademark questions from customers: pi does not advise, just notes the operational issue (e.g. “jobs held up waiting for brand permission”).
Political and election printing: no advice on legal limits; note only workload or payment problems.
Do not collect wedding guest lists, student data or names printed on corporate cards.

Chemical, solvent and machine-guarding safety: no engineering advice; if someone is hurt or there is a fire, pi stops and points to emergency services (Rescue 1122 / 15 in PK, 999/997/998 in UAE, 911 in Canada).
Staff side-printing suspicions: note as a business issue, never record named accusations.
Customer artwork may be confidential; pi does not ask for files.
build_ideas: Digital job card: each job’s stages (design, plates, print, lamination, die-cut, binding, dispatch) with status updates from the shop floor by phone.
Quote calculator: paper/board size, GSM, colours, quantity, finishing and current paper rates, producing a quote in minutes with margin shown.
Proof approval link: customer approves a specific version; the approved file and timestamp are locked to the job.
Paper and board stock register by GSM, size and brand, with reorder alerts and consumption per job.
Setting-wastage log per job and per operator, compared against an agreed allowance.
Machine board: which machine is running which job, idle time, breakdown log and spare-parts list.
Receivables tracker with ageing, advance received vs balance due, and WhatsApp reminders.
Job costing report: actual paper, plates, ink allowance, finishing and outsourced costs versus quote.
Outsourced vendor tracker for die-cutting, foiling and binding with promised and actual dates.
POD order bridge pulling Shopify/Etsy/website orders straight into the production queue with print files attached.
Counter cash and advance register that reconciles daily with the till.
Owner dashboard: open jobs, late jobs, today’s dispatches, cash collected, top customers by margin.
